candidate.educational_objective: During conventional amphotericin B therapy, monitor renal function frequently and serum electrolytes—especially potassium and magnesium—because nephrotoxicity and electrolyte depletion are important treatment toxicities.

options.A: A progressive rise in bilirubin with stable creatinine is the expected dose-limiting toxicity, so renal and electrolyte monitoring can remain routine.
options.B: A fall in fasting glucose is the characteristic toxicity of amphotericin B and should be treated as the earliest marker of treatment intolerance.
options.C: A rising creatinine with potassium or magnesium depletion is concerning for amphotericin-associated nephrotoxicity and requires close clinical review.
options.D: New mild leukocytosis with unchanged renal function is the principal expected toxicity and usually determines whether amphotericin B must be discontinued.

candidate.rationale: Conventional amphotericin B can impair renal function and is associated with electrolyte abnormalities, including hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia. Its labeling recommends frequent renal-function monitoring and regular serum-electrolyte monitoring, particularly magnesium and potassium. A rising creatinine together with potassium and magnesium depletion therefore requires prompt recognition and follow-up.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Conventional amphotericin B can reduce renal function and cause potassium/magnesium abnormalities; labeling recommends frequent renal-function and regular electrolyte monitoring.
